project.name: SilOS
project.description: Bare-metal x86_64 hobby OS kernel in Rust: async shell, FAT16 on ATA PIO, VGA text UI, Lisp interpreter, text editor.
project.runtime: no_std, freestanding, single core, ring 0, cooperative async

commands.notes: cargo run and cargo test both boot QEMU and are interactive/long-running; prefer cargo check or cargo build when only verifying compilation.

nodes.role: Kernel entry point; ordered subsystem bring-up, then spawns the shell and keyboard tasks on the executor.
notes: Separate crate from the library; refers to it as myOS:: not crate::.
Contains a leftover TEST.TXT smoke-test write on every boot.

nodes.role: Library crate root: module declarations plus the custom test harness and CPU init.
Command table, shell main loop, and every built-in command implementation.
nodes.extendHere: Add a shell command: write fn name(args: Vec<String>) -> CommandFuture, register it in init_cmds().
notes: run_cmd drops COMMANDS.lock() before invoking, enabling reentrancy from Lisp's sys form.
mkdir creates a file, not a directory.

nodes.role: Prompt line buffer and command history.
notes: getcmd splits on whitespace via split_whitespace() — this is the sole definition of the argument separator.

nodes.role: Result types returned by every command.
Tree-walking Lisp interpreter: tokenizer, reader, async evaluator, environment, standard library.
notes: eval returns Pin<Box<dyn Future>> rather than being an async fn so it can recurse — do not simplify.
sys evaluates args and calls commands::run_cmd; this is the Lisp-to-kernel bridge.
interpret splits source on ';' then pops the last fragment, so source must end with ';'.

nodes.role: Task wrapper and monotonic task IDs.
Cooperative single-core executor with a lock-free ready queue and cached wakers.
notes: No preemption: every kernel loop must await yield_now() or the machine hangs.
sleep_if_idle does cli / check / sti+hlt to avoid lost wakeups.
Ready queue capacity 100; overflow panics.

nodes.role: Scancode stream and the task that decodes scancodes into KeyEvents.
notes: add_scancode is called from the IRQ handler and must remain lock-free.
print_keypresses prints nothing despite its name.
INPUT_QUEUE and add_processed_char are dead code.

nodes.role: Global decoded-key inbox drained by whichever application is in the foreground.
notes: Exactly one consumer at a time: shell_task, run_editor or PongGame::run.

nodes.role: 80x25 VGA text terminal; home of print!/println!, colour, scrolling and hardware cursor.
notes: _print wraps access in without_interrupts to avoid deadlocking against a printing IRQ handler.
Writer::clear skips row 24.

nodes.role: Stateless random-access view of the VGA buffer, used only by Pong.
notes: Aliases 0xb8000 with WRITER; safe only because the two are never active at once.

nodes.role: UART 16550 on port 0x3F8 — how test output escapes QEMU to the host.
Polling PIO ATA driver for the primary bus, ports 0x1F0-0x1F7.
notes: Every operation busy-waits on BSY/DRQ with no timeout.
The ATA IRQ handler exists but is not used for completion.

nodes.role: FAT16 filesystem implemented directly over the ATA driver.
notes: Root directory only: no subdirectories, no long names, no delete.
8.3 names, upper-cased and space-padded by the caller.
FS is None when the disk is not valid FAT16 — all callers must handle it.
Takes IDE.lock() internally; never hold IDE.lock() across a call in here.

nodes.role: Clean shutdown: quiesce the disk, mask interrupts, try emulator power-off ports.
notes: Takes and drops FS.lock() before cli, because a spinlock held past cli could never be released.

nodes.role: GDT and TSS, including the IST stack that makes double-fault recovery possible.
notes: gdt::init() must run before interrupts::init_idt().

nodes.role: IDT setup and PIC remapping; exception and IRQ handlers.
notes: Handlers must stay lock-free beyond the lock-free queues.
LAUNCH_PONG is written by commands::pong but never read.

nodes.role: Page table access via the bootloader's physical-memory offset, and a boot-map frame allocator.
notes: allocate_frame is O(n) per call.
Frames are never freed.
translate_addr, EmptyFrameAllocator and create_example_mapping are unused tutorial leftovers.

nodes.role: Kernel heap: maps 8 MiB at 0x4444_4444_0000 and hands it to linked_list_allocator.
notes: Nothing may allocate before init_heap runs.
Dummy is an unused example allocator.

nodes.role: eden: full-screen text editor over the VGA buffer, saves on Esc.
notes: Rendering goes through the TerminalDevice trait, so the core is testable against a mock backend.
No scrolling, no quit-without-save, no 80-column clamp.
EditorModel is an unused struct hinting at the intended scrolling design.

nodes.role: Two-player Pong on the 80x25 text console.
notes: Reads raw KeyEvents to track key-down/key-up for held paddles.
wait() is a 1e6 nop spin, so speed depends on host CPU.

nodes.role: Hand-written hash map. Entirely unused — the kernel uses BTreeMap.
notes: Bug: put/remove omit the % buckets.len() that get applies; any hash >= 128 panics on insert.

flows.name: boot
flows.description: Bootloader hands off to the kernel and control ends in the executor.
steps: bootloader 0.9 → entry_point!(kernel_main) with &'static BootInfo
myOS::init(): gdt::init → interrupts::init_idt → PICS.initialize → sti
memory::init(phys_mem_offset) → OffsetPageTable
BootInfoFrameAllocator::init(&boot_info.memory_map)
allocator::init_heap → alloc is usable from this point on
fat16::init() reads LBA 0 and validates the BPB
commands::init_cmds() populates the COMMANDS table
Executor::new + spawn(print_keypresses) + spawn(shell_task) + run() — never returns

flows.name: keystroke
flows.description: A physical key press reaching an application.
steps: IRQ1 → interrupts::keyboard_interrupt_handler reads port 0x60
task::keyboard::add_scancode pushes onto lock-free SCANCODE_QUEUE and wakes WAKER
task::keyboard::print_keypresses polls ScancodeStream and decodes via pc_keyboard
KeyEvent pushed onto input::KEY_EVENT_QUEUE
foreground consumer calls input::pop_key(): shell_task, run_editor or PongGame::run
consumer runs its own pc_keyboard decoder to get DecodedKey (Pong uses KeyEvent directly)

flows.name: command-execution
flows.description: A typed line becoming a running command.
steps: shell_task echoes characters and accumulates them into SHELL
Enter sets COMMAND_PENDING
SHELL::getcmd splits the line on whitespace via split_whitespace()
commands::run_cmd clones the Arc from COMMANDS and releases the lock
the returned CommandFuture is awaited by shell_task
Success.success_code is printed only when print_code is true; ProcessError always prints

flows.name: file-write
steps: caller pads a name into 8.3 form ([u8;8], [u8;3]), upper-cased
FS.lock() → Fat16FileSystem::write_new_file or overwrite_file
overwrite_file frees the existing cluster chain first
find_free_cluster scans the FAT; set_fat_entry links the chain
cluster_to_lba converts to an LBA; ide::write_sector_bytes issues ATA 0x30 per sector
the directory entry is written back with the new first cluster and size

flows.name: lisp-syscall
flows.description: Lisp reaching back into the kernel.
steps: commands::interpret builds a default_env and injects every command name as a Symbol
numeric/boolean script args are bound to n0/n1 and b0/b1
source is split on ';' (the final fragment is discarded) and each statement is parse_eval'd
eval encounters (sys ...) → evaluates and stringifies the args
commands::run_cmd is called reentrantly and its future is awaited
the result becomes RispExp::Syscall, or a RispErr on failure

invariants.rule: Nothing may allocate before allocator::init_heap runs.
Every long-running loop must await task::executor::yield_now(); there is no preemption.
Interrupt handlers must not take spinlocks beyond the lock-free queues.
Lock order is FS then IDE, never the reverse; fat16 methods take IDE.lock() internally.
Never hold a spinlock across interrupts::disable(); it could never be released.
Access to WRITER from interruptible code goes through without_interrupts.
run_cmd releases COMMANDS.lock() before invoking so commands can recurse.
gdt::init() must precede interrupts::init_idt() because of the double-fault IST entry.
Only one application drains input::KEY_EVENT_QUEUE at a time.

tests.proves: println! works on a bare boot with no subsystem init
heap allocation, reallocation and reuse of freed memory
the double-fault IST catches a guard-page hit instead of triple-faulting
a failing assertion is detected as a panic
inline #[test_case]s: println output, scrolling, buffer contents

steps: Write fn my_cmd(args: Vec<String>) -> CommandFuture returning Box::pin(async move { ... }).
args[0] is the command name; real arguments start at args[1].
Return Ok(Success { success_code, print_code }) or Err(ProcessError { error_code }).
Register it in init_cmds() with c.insert(String::from("my_cmd"), Arc::new(my_cmd)).
It becomes callable from Lisp via (sys my_cmd ...) automatically.
For a pure function: add a data.insert(...) with RispExp::Func in default_env().
For a form needing lazy evaluation or env access: add a match arm in eval's `match s.as_str()`.
Document it in docs/lisp.md and add it to the builtins/specialForms list in docs/project-graph.json.
Write an async fn returning ().
executor.spawn(Task::new(my_task())) in kernel_main before executor.run().
Ensure every loop iteration awaits yield_now().
Add the method to impl Fat16FileSystem, taking IDE.lock() internally as the existing methods do.
Expose it as a command in commands.rs, handling the FS == None case with 'File system not mounted'.
Remember names are 8.3, upper-cased and space-padded.
Add a variant to InterruptIndex with the correct PIC-offset vector.
Write extern "x86-interrupt" fn handler(_stack_frame: InterruptStackFrame).
Register it in the IDT lazy_static.
End with PICS.lock().notify_end_of_interrupt(...) for hardware IRQs.
Keep the body lock-free — enqueue work for a task instead of doing it inline.
